segments.g0: Two numbers on your DiaBite receipt can look alike, but they answer different questions.
segments.g1: The glycemic index, or GI, tells you how fast a food raises blood sugar.
segments.g2: But GI says nothing about how much you eat. That is what glycemic load, or GL, adds: the index and the portion together. It tells you how much a meal raises it.
segments.g3: Here is one slice of rye bread, thirty-five grams. Fourteen point two grams of available carbohydrate. GI fifty. Glycemic load seven point one.
segments.g4: Now two slices, seventy grams. The index is still fifty. But the load doubles, to fourteen point two.
segments.g5: Same bread, same GI, twice the effect. That is why the portion matters.
segments.g6: On the receipt, read each food's portion and available carbohydrate first, then its GI, then its load. The load is the figure that adds up across a meal.
segments.g7: DiaBite is a reference tool. It does not replace your care team.
